chunks: Torque is current, speed is voltage. The question: What electrical parameter corresponds to high torque? Why? What about high RPM?
For a DC motor, torque follows current, and speed follows voltage. More current through the winding gives more twisting force.
More voltage lets the motor spin faster before its back-EMF catches up with the supply. This is the simplest way to think about what a motor controller is doing.
Think of a treadmill you are running on. You choose the belt speed with a dial: that is the voltage.
How hard you have to push to keep up depends on the incline or load: that is the current and torque. A steeper hill means more effort at the same speed.
The analogy has a gap: on a real motor, a heavier load also slows the speed a little.
The electrical port (V, R, L) in series with a back-EMF source E that stands for the mechanical side. Current through that source sets the torque; its voltage is set by the speed.
Torque ( T ): the twisting force, in newton-meters (N·m). It is current times a motor constant: T equals K tI . Back-EMF ( E ): the voltage the spinning motor makes.
It is speed omega (in radians per second, rad/s) times a motor constant: E equals K e omega .
Voltage balance: the supply voltage equals the drop across the winding's resistance ( IR ) plus the back-EMF. Stall: shaft held still, so the current is maximum.
PWM duty: switching the supply on and off very fast; the fraction of time it is on sets the average voltage.
Use a 12 volts motor with R equals 1 ohms and K t equals K e equals 0. 02 . At 0. 5 amps, the torque is 0. 02 times 0. 5 = 0. 01 N·m, and the speed is (12 minus 0. 5 times 1) / 0.
02 = 575 rad/s . Load it to 5 amps, and the torque is 0. 1 N·m, ten times more. The speed drops to (12 minus 5) / 0. 02 = 350 rad/s .
That is the whole idea: current sets torque, and voltage (minus the IR drop) sets speed.
"Torque goes with current and speed goes with voltage.
The Lorentz force on the winding gives T equals K tI , so more current means more torque; that's why stall, the highest torque, is also the highest current, V over R .
Spinning generates a back-EMF K e omega that opposes the supply, so omega about (V minus IR) over K e : speed tracks voltage, minus a load-dependent drop.
K t and K e are the same number in SI units, by energy conservation."
